title: Abdominal examination: hepatosplenomegaly
stem: Cubicle 33. Mr Ng, 58, has increasing abdominal swelling and ankle oedema. Perform an abdominal examination and present your findings.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: Peripheral stigmata first, then the abdomen: liver, spleen, ascites.

phases.title: Present
phases.goal: The diagnosis and the next tests.

notes:
Checked against standard abdominal examination technique and BSG/EASL guidance on decompensated cirrhosis and ascites.

Sequence: introduce, consent, position flat with one pillow, expose (nipples to knees with dignity); general inspection; hands (clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema, Dupuytren's, asterixis); arms (bruising, scratch marks); face and eyes (jaundice, pallor, xanthelasma, parotid swelling); neck (Virchow's node); chest (spider naevi, gynaecomastia); abdomen inspection (distension, caput medusae, scars); palpation (light, deep, liver from the right iliac fossa up with breathing, spleen from the right iliac fossa toward the left costal margin, kidneys ballotable); percussion (liver span, splenic dullness, shifting dullness for ascites); auscultation (bowel sounds, bruits); complete with hernial orifices, external genitalia and PR (offer), legs (oedema).

Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly with ascites and stigmata suggest cirrhosis with portal hypertension. Spleen vs kidney: the spleen has a notch, moves down and medially with inspiration, you cannot get above it, dull to percussion. Ascites: diagnostic tap (cell count for SBP — neutrophils > 250/mm³, albumin for SAAG, culture), salt restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide, large-volume paracentesis with albumin. Your notes list hepatosplenomegaly as a Surgical gym topic without detail.

Perfect script checked against standard abdominal examination and BSG ascites guidance, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the spleen trap; the liver and spleen close-ups now show palpation.

steps.label: Examine the abdomen
steps.hint: Hands, face, chest, then abdomen: inspect, palpate (liver, spleen, kidneys), percuss (shifting dullness), auscultate, complete.

Peripheries.t: Hands: nails, palms; hold your arms out for a flap
Peripheries.r: Leuconychia, palmar erythema, Dupuytren's contracture; no flap.
Peripheries.mark: Examines the hands for liver stigmata

Peripheries.r: Icteric sclerae; left supraclavicular fossa normal.
Peripheries.mark: Looks for jaundice and Virchow's node

Abdomen.r: Distended with dilated periumbilical veins, everted umbilicus.

Abdomen.t: Palpate the liver from the right iliac fossa upwards with his breathing
Abdomen.r: Liver edge 3 cm below the costal margin, firm, irregular.

Abdomen.t: Palpate the spleen from the right iliac fossa toward the left costal margin
Abdomen.r: Spleen tip 4 cm below the left costal margin, moves with breathing, notch felt.
Dullness in the flanks shifts when he rolls to his right: ascites.
Abdomen.do: percuss flank > say roll-R,roll-L > percuss flank

Abdomen.mark: Auscultates for bowel sounds and bruits

Complete.t: To complete: the legs, and I'd offer the hernial orifices, genitalia and a rectal examination
Complete.do: press shin | look legs | feel groin

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings.
steps.label: Present
steps.hint: Summarise: chronic liver disease with portal hypertension; investigations; SBP.

opts.t: Stigmata of chronic liver disease, with hepatosplenomegaly and ascites: cirrhosis with portal hypertension.
opts.mark: Presents a coherent summary and diagnosis

opts.t: A diagnostic ascitic tap for cell count, SBP, albumin for the SAAG, and culture; LFTs, clotting and an ultrasound.

options: Janeway lesions, Roth spots and a new murmur

script.say: Hands: nails, palms; hold your arms out for a flap. Eyes, face and neck. The chest.
script.do: Leuconychia, palmar erythema, Dupuytren's contracture; no flap. Icteric sclerae; left supraclavicular fossa normal. Five spider naevi; gynaecomastia.

script.say: Inspect the abdomen. Palpate the liver from the right iliac fossa upwards with his breathing. Palpate the spleen from the right iliac fossa toward the left costal margin.
script.do: Distended with dilated periumbilical veins, everted umbilicus. Liver edge 3 cm below the costal margin, firm, irregular. Spleen tip 4 cm below the left costal margin, moves with breathing, notch felt.

script.say: Shifting dullness. Auscultate. To complete: the legs, and I'd offer the hernial orifices, genitalia and a rectal examination.
script.do: Dullness in the flanks shifts when he rolls to his right: ascites. Bowel sounds normal; no bruits. Pitting oedema to mid-shin.

script.say: Stigmata of chronic liver disease, with hepatosplenomegaly and ascites: cirrhosis with portal hypertension. A diagnostic ascitic tap for cell count, SBP, albumin for the SAAG, and culture; LFTs, clotting and an ultrasound.
